title: On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies
relevance: Foundational clock synchronization and frame-dependent simultaneity; baseline to reproduce.
limits: Translation page screened; no theorem-level extraction yet. Does not itself settle temporal ontology.

title: On Logical Analysis of Relativity Theories
relevance: Existing logical axiom analysis of relativity; essential prior art for assumption-dependency proposals.
limits: Formal systems and independence results not yet extracted or reproduced.

title: Physlib: formalized physics in Lean
relevance: Reuse candidate for formal physics; repository descends from PhysLean.
limits: README-level inspection only. No commit pinned, API audited, dependency installed, or local proof built.

title: Towards Formal Verification of Computations and Hypercomputations in Relativistic Physics
relevance: Prior machine-assisted axiomatic relativity in Isabelle/HOL; Lean is not the beginning of this subject.
limits: Repository text screened, implementation and precise verified results not audited.

title: Simultaneity in Minkowski spacetime: from uniqueness to arbitrariness
relevance: Existing constructive results on simultaneity definability and observer data; close predecessor to an assumption atlas.
limits: Exact theorem hypotheses and relation to later work require full-text reading.

title: Presentism as an empirical hypothesis
relevance: A proposed empirical presentism that challenges a shared starting assumption of standard debate; guards against dismissing every presentist variant together.
limits: Author abstract describes the proposal; no independent endorsement or proof audit. DOI 10.1086/673897.

title: A Classical Sequential Growth Dynamics for Causal Sets
relevance: Covariant stochastic growth models give a concrete arena for studying growth and history representations.
limits: Classical model family, not established quantum gravity or proof of objective passage.

title: What becomes of a causal set
relevance: Studies possible forms of becoming in causal sets and interpretive costs; close philosophical prior art.
limits: Exact constructions and constraints still require full-text extraction.

title: Problem of Time in Quantum Gravity
relevance: Maps multiple distinct problems of time, including foliation and observables; useful routing rather than a single frozen-equation slogan.
limits: Review is not evidence that any proposed quantum-gravity solution is empirically established.

title: Spacetime Quantum Reference Frames and superpositions of proper times
relevance: Relational clock construction and quantum reference-frame descriptions; candidate baseline for a precise extension.
limits: Model-specific quantum predictions; does not establish a universal temporal ontology.

title: Bell's Theorem for Temporal Order
relevance: A quantitative route to challenging classical temporal order under specified assumptions.
limits: Theoretical proposal here; no claim that a gravity-mediated experiment has realized it or that it refutes all presentism.

title: Measurement events relative to temporal quantum reference frames
relevance: Compares temporal measurement approaches within Page-Wootters and operational interpretation.
limits: Need exact idealizations and later equivalence/measurement results before identifying a gap.

title: Data Tables for Lorentz and CPT Violation
relevance: 2026 edition provides a route from specific symmetry-violating physical models to existing experimental bounds.
limits: No coefficient bounds extracted. An unobservable preferred structure is not automatically constrained by these measurements.

title: Axioms for physical reasoning: codifying the Seiberg--Witten solution in Lean
relevance: Authors separate named physical postulates from machine-checked consequences; relevant methodology for explicit premises.
limits: Authors' report only. No repository build, axiom audit, or correspondence check performed here.

title: Multi-agent Autoformalization of Tensor Network Theory
relevance: Direct prior art for LLM subagents formalizing theoretical physics; inspect workflow and reusable artifacts.
limits: Multi-agent method and claimed results not independently evaluated here; using a swarm alone is not novel.

title: AxQM: A Textbook-Scale Benchmark for Formal Proof Synthesis in a Library of Finite-Dimensional Quantum Mechanics
relevance: Potential finite-dimensional quantum formalization resources and verification criteria for proof synthesis.
limits: Benchmark and libraries not audited. Kernel checking cannot establish natural-language correspondence by itself.

title: LLMs with in-context learning for Algorithmic Theoretical Physics
relevance: LLM plus Maple case study in cosmological perturbations; compare CAS-assisted reproduction with proof formalization.
limits: Authors report successes and failure modes on selected tasks; not validation of general autonomous physics discovery.

title: Can Theoretical Physics Research Benefit from Language Agents?
relevance: Prior work on language agents in theoretical physics; candidate methodology comparator.
limits: Version-specific workflow, benchmark scope, and failure rates need full-text audit.

title: Is Exact Markovianity Fundamental Once Time Is Relational?
relevance: Authors propose finite-resolution relational clocks and effective open-system dynamics; a tractable recent-result audit candidate.
limits: Claim not reproduced. Must trace clock assumptions and older imperfect-clock/decoherence literature before treating this as new.

title: On the (Non)Unitarity with respect to the Clock of a Dynamical Local Observer and the Einstein Equivalence Principle
relevance: Authors compare observer-clock evolution in fixed backgrounds and dynamical gravity; potential assumptions-focused comparison target.
limits: Conditional physical claims require full-text review, reproduction, and comparison with existing clock frameworks.

title: The Trinity of Relational Quantum Dynamics
relevance: Establishes equivalence among three relational quantum descriptions, including treatment of non-ideal clocks. Crucial prior art that narrows candidate B.
limits: Exact allowed clock classes and interaction assumptions need full-text audit. Non-ideal clocks as a broad topic are already covered; do not call them an unexplored extension.

title: Equivalence of approaches to relational quantum dynamics in relativistic settings
relevance: Extends relational-dynamics equivalence sector-wise to relativistic systems; important existing bridge between frameworks.
limits: Frequency sectors, covariant POVMs and precise hypotheses must be retained in any reuse or proposed extension.
